title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, 50, of Tennessee, was arrested at gunpoint by US marshals in July 2025 at her home while she was babysitting four children. She was falsely charged in Fargo, North Dakota, with four counts of unauthorized use of personal identifying information and four counts of theft. She spent about six months in custody, nearly four months in a county jail without bail and about two more months in North Dakota. The charges were dropped after her lawyer gave bank records showing she was in Tennessee when the Fargo fraud happened. She was released on Christmas Eve.

Lipps has sued the city of Fargo and detective Lucas Heck for $10m. She says police wrongly relied on an AI facial recognition system, which returned her social media photo as a potential lead from a fake ID used by a suspect. She says she did not look like the suspect and had never been to North Dakota. Lawsuit alleges the detective did not investigate further before requesting an arrest warrant. A Fargo spokesperson said the city does not comment on pending litigation.
